newsitem.title: DUBAI: Abu Dhabi seeks Neste stake in Borealis.
newsitem.headline: Abu Dhabi seeks Neste stake in Borealis.

text.p: Abu Dhabi's International Petroleum Investment Company (IPIC) is moving to take a 50 percent stake in Scandinavian petrochemical firm Borealis, an Abu Dhabi government-owned newspaper said on Wednesday.

"Substantial progress has been made by IPIC in its quest to acquire a 50 percent stake in the Scandinavian petrochemical firm Borealis from Finland's Neste Oy," the English-language Emirates News paper said.
Borealis is 50-50 owned by Finnish energy group Neste Oy and Norwegian Statoil.
The Scandinavian firm in June secured a 40 percent stake in a venture with the state-owned Abu Dhabi National Oil Company (ADNOC) to build a petrochemical plant in Abu Dhabi.
IPIC is a wholly-owned subsidiary of ADNOC.

"The Borealis stake will enable ADNOC to make inroads into the competitive energy market of Europe. Negotiations have reached the point where IPIC will be going ahead with the buy-out," the paper quoted an unnamed industry source.
"Industry officials said buying into Borealis would also enable Abu Dhabi to expand oil exports to European refineries," Emirates News reported.
However, "a lot of the fine print of the agreement has yet to be agreed up," the same source told Emirates News.
The petrochemical plant, valued at around $1 billion will have a 450,000 tonnes a year polyethylene capacity and start-up is planned for the year 2000.
Abu Dhabi is one of the seven emirates that make up the oil-rich United Arab Emirates (UAE)
